name: Coffee-maker pathways
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
native_basis: element release from the food-contact alloy into food or food simulant (µg/kg food)
native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE FOOD-CONTACT ALLOY INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, µg/kg of food, determined against an acidic simulant at the article's stated use temperature and duration with the third successive release governing for repeat-use articles. This is a RELEASE basis on the food, not the plastics-simulant convention and not a total-content basis: the percent-by-weight lead limits on food-contact metals and solder are a separate MATERIAL-CONTENT obligation, disclosed as companions and never published here.
scope_note: The full WETTED PATHWAY of a beverage-brewing appliance, from reservoir to cup, taken as a system rather than as a single material. The row is a control because the pathway is dominated by components in material families for which no credible sovereign sets an element release ceiling: aluminium and copper boilers, brass and leaded-brass fittings and group heads, and plated wetted parts. Two conditions make this row harsher than a storage article and are written into the component plan: the water is HOT and often near-boiling and is held in contact with the boiler and fittings, and DESCALING with acid is a manufacturer-instructed periodic condition that strips passivation and mobilises metal, so the release test must include a post-descaling draw. Polymeric reservoirs, carafes and tubing are bound by the plastics migration ceilings directly or by disclosed read-across as separate components, and the sovereign drinking-water parametric values are disclosed as WATER-basis companions on the beverage, never as this row's release ceilings. TRACEABILITY OF THE COMPONENT POINTER: where this row's component plan refers a plastic component to "the plastics migration ceilings", that phrase resolves to a concrete published set of values inside this same standard and is not an unresolved pointer. It means the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II values published on this category's plastics rows — eu_10_2011_pb_sml_nd (lead, not detectable at 10 ug/kg food), eu_10_2011_cd_sml_nd (cadmium, 2), eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd (total arsenic, 10), eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd (total mercury, 10), eu_10_2011_ni_sml (nickel, 20), eu_10_2011_al_sml (aluminium, 1000) and eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd (total chromium, not detectable at 10), with tin excepted because the instrument lists no tin entry. Those values bind the plastic component as a SEPARATE obligation in its own material family and are never this row's published ceiling, which stays in this row's own native basis.
material: Plastic water reservoirs and carafe bodies; silicone and EPDM tubing; aluminium and copper boilers and thermoblocks; brass and leaded-brass fittings, valves and group heads; stainless steel heater tubes and portafilters; nickel-plated and chrome-plated wetted parts; aluminium moka pots.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) first-draw and steady-state brewed-water sampling through the assembled appliance, against a matched influent blank; (2) BOILER or thermoblock interior, aluminium and copper configurations as their own lots; (3) BRASS and leaded-brass fittings, valves and group heads, alloy composition verified for lead; (4) POST-DESCALING draw, sampled immediately after the manufacturer's stated descaling procedure and again after the stated flush; (5) silicone and EPDM tubing, under the polymer regime by disclosed read-across; (6) plastic reservoir and carafe, under the plastics migration ceilings; (7) plated and stainless wetted parts, including any solder or braze; (8) aluminium moka pots and stovetop brewers as their own lot.
basis_guard: element release|specific release|specific release limit|release into food|release into a food simulant|release into the food simulant|acetic acid
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as element RELEASE from a metal or alloy food-contact surface into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap. DECLARED VACUOUS STATE (recorded, not overlooked): as written this guard matches ZERO live, non-draft and non-quarantined rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and that is its intended state. The release regime this row's basis family belongs to is not in the register in any form this row may bind, which is the same fact this row's control cells record and state in detail; a guard that admitted a live row today could only do so by admitting a foreign basis. The guard is nevertheless expressed in the register's own basis vocabulary (element or specific release, release into food or a food simulant, 4 percent acetic acid extract, per dm2 of food-contact surface, net device contribution to the treated water) so that a future correct ingest of that regime BINDS through it. The previous prose-sentence guard on this row would have REJECTED the very instruments it was waiting for and forced them to a gap, which is the defect this rewrite removes. Two limits on the guard's force are stated plainly rather than left implicit: the compiler returns on the control branch before basis resolution, so a guard is never evaluated on a control cell, and this note rather than the machine is what carries the guard's force on this row today. The engine change that would close that hole - an assertion that every declared basis_guard either matches at least one live register row or carries basis_guard_vacuous_by_design, failing the build otherwise - is recorded as a tooling gap and is outside this config's scope.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a numeric ceiling on element release from a metal or alloy food-contact article. Regulation (EU) 10/2011 governs plastics only; metals and alloys are a separate Regulation 1935/2004 Annex I material family for which the EU has adopted no specific measure, the US regulates food-contact substances without an element release ceiling, and Codex, FSANZ, Health Canada, the UK and Hong Kong set none. Testing is therefore mandatory on every certified lot with no invented ceiling: a limit borrowed from the plastics regulation would be a limit written for a different material family, and for an alloy surface the plastics nickel and aluminium values are not even achievable, so borrowing them would be an unfounded number rather than a stricter one. Lead in a food-contact metal article arrives from the alloy, from lead-bearing solder and brazing at joints and base plugs, and from plated or printed decoration on the interior. Japan Notice 370 (1959) and Korea MFDS Notice 2024-29 do set sovereign lead limits for food-contact metals, but they are percent-by-weight limits on the metal, solder and tin plating: a MATERIAL-CONTENT basis. Both jurisdictions also sit OUTSIDE the HMTc credible-regulator set used for anchoring in this build, so they could not supply a published number here even in the right basis; they are disclosed as real foreign obligations and must not be promoted to anchors without a recorded governance ruling. That obligation is disclosed as a companion and is verified on every certified article; it is not published as this row's release ceiling, because a content limit and a release limit are different measured quantities. The binding component on this row is normally a brass fitting or an aluminium or copper boiler, and the binding CONDITION is the post-descaling draw; a cold-reservoir or first-brew result does not represent the appliance.
Pb.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact metal component under worst foreseeable use conditions (acidic simulant at the article's stated cooking or holding temperature and duration; for repeat-use articles the third successive release result governs), ICP-MS determination in the simulant, plus alloy-composition verification of every food-contact component by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only).

A not-material determination is therefore not available here and the fail-safe applies: inorganic arsenic is a control, tested and escalated alongside total arsenic. MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains. A metal or alloy food-contact surface contains no organic matrix and no methylation pathway, and no credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for any food-contact material. Total mercury is the governing determination for this row and remains a mandatory control; methylmercury is not material and never substitutes for it. This row includes a standing cold-water reservoir, so the wetted-niche question is addressed rather than assumed away: the reservoir and the wetted path are bare polymer and alloy surfaces with no carbon-rich or adsorbent medium, are drawn down and refilled in normal use, and hold no bioavailable inorganic-mercury pool, so no persistent anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing niche capable of methylating mercury is established. Where a machine incorporates a carbon or ion-exchange water-treatment cartridge, that component is a water-treatment device and routes to the water-filter rows, where methylmercury is a CONTROL rather than a not-material determination.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury release determination per the tHg control; reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS only where total mercury is detected in the release extract.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for a food-contact material or article in any basis. The metallic mercury impurity route in an alloy produces no organomercury species.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the health-relevant chromium species and it cannot be dismissed on a metal article: chromate conversion coatings, passivation treatments and chromate-bearing pigments in interior printing are live sources, and hot alkaline conditions can oxidise chromium(III) at the surface. No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium release ceiling for a food-contact metal article, and this row's total-chromium cell is itself a control, so no published parent bounds this species and a speciation-bounded not-material determination is unavailable. The fail-safe applies. No credible sovereign sets a numeric ceiling on element release from a metal or alloy food-contact article. Cr-VI.reference_method: Food-simulant release testing on each food-contact metal component under worst foreseeable use conditions (acidic simulant at the article's stated cooking or holding temperature and duration; for repeat-use articles the third successive release result governs), ICP-MS determination in the simulant, plus alloy-composition verification of every food-contact component by ICP-OES after acid digestion (XRF for screening only).
